bustools.label: bustools
bustools.description: Process Barcode, UMI and Set (BUS) records from single-cell RNA sequencing. Run the numbered commands in order to correct cell barcodes and produce a gene-count matrix.
bustools.argumentsHelp: The first entry is a bustools command, such as sort or count. Do not include the bustools program name. Sorting uses one thread and a bounded memory budget.

sort.label: 1. Sort BUS records
sort.description: Sort the supplied BUS records by cell barcode, UMI and equivalence class. Each output remains available to the next command.

correct.label: 2. Correct cell barcodes
correct.description: Correct the sorted records against the supplied barcode on-list. Run the first sorting step before this command.

resort.label: 3. Sort corrected records
resort.description: Barcode correction can change record order. Sort the corrected BUS file before counting molecules.

count.label: 4. Count molecules by gene
count.description: Use transcript names, equivalence classes and the transcript-to-gene map to create a sparse cell-by-gene matrix and its barcode and gene labels.

inspect.label: Inspect corrected BUS records
inspect.description: Write a JSON summary of the sorted, corrected records, including barcode and UMI statistics.

text.label: View corrected BUS records as text
text.description: Export the corrected barcode, UMI, equivalence class and count fields for inspection. The BUS file remains binary and unchanged.

compress.label: Compress sorted BUS records
compress.description: Losslessly compress the sorted, corrected records to the BUSZ format.

inflate.label: Restore compressed BUS records
inflate.description: Restore the BUS file from records.busz. Run the compression command first.

help.label: Command help
help.description: Show sort options. Replace sort with another command name to view its help.

bustools.label: Mouse single-cell RNA-seq BUS records
bustools.description: BUS records from a real mouse single-cell RNA-seq experiment (SRR8599150, 10x v2), with matching transcript, gene and barcode reference files. See the data documentation for its source and selection.
